status_detail: The exposure is a prescription drug and the population is a condition-code phenotype tightened with a concurrent antibiotic course, so this study is not blocked by the inputevents ETL gap (see docs/validation_question_bank.md, F1-F7). Remaining work before a run: (1) human approval of the systemic-corticosteroid concept set and the severe-CAP phenotype (condition + antibiotic + severity marker); (2) generation and clinical review of a candidate DAG against reference_dag.json; (3) a positive-predictive-value check on the pneumonia phenotype; (4) confirming the non-CAP-steroid-indication exclusions. Question bank id: Q8.
source_question: Among adults admitted to the ICU with severe community-acquired pneumonia, what is the effect of starting a systemic corticosteroid within 48 hours of admission, versus no systemic corticosteroid in that window, on in-hospital all-cause mortality?

anchor_trial.name: CAPE COD
anchor_trial.citation: Dequin PF, Meziani F, Quenot JP, et al. Hydrocortisone in Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia. N Engl J Med. 2023;388(21):1931-1941.
anchor_trial.design: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, 31 French ICUs, 800 patients with severe CAP.

supporting_syntheses.citation: Efficacy and safety of adjunctive corticosteroids in the treatment of severe community-acquired pneumonia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Crit Care. 2023;27:274.
supporting_syntheses.note: 7 RCTs, 1,689 patients. Day-30 mortality RR 0.61 (95% CI 0.44-0.85); less mechanical ventilation RR 0.57 (0.45-0.73).

supporting_syntheses.citation: Torres A, Sibila O, Ferrer M, et al. Effect of corticosteroids on treatment failure among hospitalized patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia and high inflammatory response: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2015;313(7):677-686.

Blum CA, Nigro N, Briel M, et al. Adjunct prednisone therapy for patients with community-acquired pneumonia: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial. Lancet. 2015;385(9977):1511-1518.

counter_weight.citation: Meduri GU, Shih MC, Bridges L, et al. Low-dose methylprednisolone treatment in critically ill patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia (ESCAPe). Intensive Care Med. 2022;48(8):1009-1023.
counter_weight.note: No 60-day mortality benefit in a predominantly older male VA population.

data_source: runtime-configured restricted OMOP dataset (MIMIC-IV v2.2 -> OMOP CDM 5.3.1, OHDSI/MIMIC ETL)

target_trial.population: Adults admitted to the ICU with severe community-acquired pneumonia
target_trial.treatment: A systemic corticosteroid (hydrocortisone, methylprednisolone, prednisone, prednisolone, dexamethasone) ordered within 48 hours of hospital admission
target_trial.comparator: No systemic corticosteroid ordered within 48 hours of hospital admission
target_trial.time_zero: Hospital admission (the first inpatient visit of the qualifying encounter); the exposure-ascertainment window is the first 48 hours after it
secondary_estimands: ATE on new hyperglycaemia within 7 days (glucose >= 180 mg/dL or a new insulin order) - positive control for a real corticosteroid effect
ATE on the initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation after time zero (among those not ventilated at baseline)
CATE by baseline shock (vasopressor exposure at time zero) vs no shock
eligibility_criteria: Community-acquired pneumonia recorded within 48 hours of admission (condition code), tightened by a concurrent antibiotic course started within 48 hours; hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia codes are excluded, as are aspiration-pneumonia-only codes
Severe: ICU admission within 48 hours of hospital admission, OR vasopressor or invasive mechanical ventilation within 48 hours
First qualifying pneumonia admission per patient only
No systemic corticosteroid order in the 30 days before admission (new-user)

No competing systemic-corticosteroid indication documented at baseline: COPD or asthma exacerbation as the primary reason for admission, active autoimmune or inflammatory disease on maintenance steroids, adrenal insufficiency, recent solid-organ transplant, or a haematological malignancy on a steroid-containing chemotherapy protocol. A sensitivity analysis relaxing the COPD exclusion (adjusting for COPD instead) is prespecified.
target_trial.assignment_procedure: Not randomized; the decision to give a systemic corticosteroid is the treating team's, driven by perceived severity, the inflammatory picture, and any airway component. An observational target-trial emulation.
target_trial.censoring_strategy: For the in-hospital primary outcome, administrative censoring at hospital discharge. For the 30-day secondary, administrative censoring at the earlier of the end of observation or 30 days after time zero.
target_trial.analysis_strategy: Intention-to-treat analog: exposure status is fixed by a corticosteroid order in the 48-hour window and not updated afterward. A per-protocol sensitivity analysis requiring at least 3 consecutive days of corticosteroid is prespecified.
target_trial.treatment_value: Systemic corticosteroid started within 48 hours of hospital admission
target_trial.comparator_value: No systemic corticosteroid within 48 hours of hospital admission

design_constraints: This is the bank's clearest sensitivity test: the RCTs and a 7-trial meta-analysis agree on a mortality benefit in the severe stratum (risk difference roughly -3 to -6 percentage points). If the pipeline returns a null here it is too conservative.
Confounding by indication runs toward the null or toward harm (steroids are given to the sicker patient), so a recovered protective effect is a conservative demonstration, not an overstatement.

COPD is the single most important confounder: COPD patients with pneumonia receive steroids for the airway component and have a different baseline mortality. Exclude COPD-exacerbation-primary admissions; adjust for COPD as a comorbidity in the main model and test the relaxed-exclusion sensitivity analysis.
Baseline inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein, white cell count) and severity (SOFA, PaO2/FiO2, lactate) must be ascertained strictly before time zero.
Calendar year is a confounder: corticosteroid practice in CAP shifted across 2008-2019 (notably after the 2015 Blum and Torres trials).
New hyperglycaemia is a positive control - a real, expected corticosteroid effect. If it does not come out clearly positive, the covariate/outcome plumbing is wrong.
Do not promote text-matched drug or condition names to executable concept sets without human review.

systemic_corticosteroid.note: Approve RxNorm ingredient seeds plus concept_ancestor descendants. Restrict to systemic routes (oral, intravenous, intramuscular); exclude inhaled, topical, ophthalmic, intra-articular, and rectal formulations. Fludrocortisone is excluded from the primary (mineralocorticoid). Hydrocortisone given purely as stress-dose steroid for refractory shock is in-scope but should be flagged in the per-protocol analysis.

community_acquired_pneumonia.note: PPV is the main risk. Tighten with a concurrent antibiotic course within 48 h. Exclude 'Ventilator associated pneumonia', 'Hospital acquired pneumonia', 'Pneumonitis due to aspiration' (unless co-coded with a bacterial pneumonia). A chest-imaging procedure within 48 h is an optional additional requirement for a high-specificity sensitivity analysis.

systemic_antibiotic.note: Used only to tighten the pneumonia phenotype (a concurrent antibiotic course started within 48 h of admission), not as an exposure or comparator.

PaO2/FiO2 ratio or lowest SpO2/FiO2 on day one

published_benchmarks.source: CAPE COD, NEJM 2023;388(21):1931-1941, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2215145; meta-analysis Crit Care 2023;27:274, doi:10.1186/s13054-023-04561-z. Read the exact figures from the primary texts before scoring.
published_benchmarks.expected_pipeline_result: A genuine protective effect: risk difference roughly -3 to -6 percentage points in this severe stratum. New hyperglycaemia should come out clearly positive. Returning a null for mortality would indicate the pipeline is too conservative.

feasibility_checklist.F1_exposure_is_drug_or_coded_procedure: PASS - all five corticosteroids are well-mapped prescriptions.
feasibility_checklist.F2_ever_exposed_in_window_is_enough: PASS - a corticosteroid order in the 48 h window defines the exposure; a per-protocol >=3-day analysis is secondary.
feasibility_checklist.F4_outcome_reliably_captured: PASS - in-hospital and 30-day mortality from the death record; hyperglycaemia from measurement.
feasibility_checklist.F5_population_phenotype: WARN - CAP is a condition-code phenotype; PPV depends on the concurrent-antibiotic requirement and the exclusion of HAP/VAP/aspiration-only codes. Run a PPV check before committing.
feasibility_checklist.F6_adequate_n_and_followup: PASS - severe-CAP ICU cohort roughly 5,000-8,000; corticosteroid-treated fraction roughly 25-40%.
feasibility_checklist.F7_confounders_measurable: PASS - severity, inflammatory markers, comorbidity history, pathogen, vasopressor/ventilation status, care_site, calendar year. Radiographic extent is not captured (see reference_dag.json).
